result.title: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
result.summary: Recent advances in interactive world models have made it possible to generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs. Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data. Existing gameplay video datasets typically consist of clips under ten seconds, with captions that describe whole clips in coarse and undifferentiated text, which is insufficient for controllable long-horizon generation. We address this with GameVerse, a minute-scale gameplay video dataset purpose-built for long-horizon interactive world modeling. GameVerse contains 69.7K clips spanning 1,655 hours and 349.6 million frames across diverse first- and third-person gameplay, including 1,358 hours of continuous two-minute sequences, an order of magnitude longer than prior datasets. Clips pass through a unified pipeline of scene-consistent segmentation, quality filtering, camera pose estimation, and event-based caption annotation. Each clip is paired with a temporally stable camera trajectory that remains coherent across minutes, together with captions that separate static scene context from dynamic foreground events and align to event boundaries rather than fixed time windows. Comprehensive analysis shows that GameVerse surpasses existing public datasets in scale, diversity, and annotation quality. Experiments further demonstrate that training on GameVerse substantially extends the temporal horizon of interactive world models.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GameVerse，一个面向长时程交互式世界建模的分钟级 gameplay 视频数据集（69.7K 片段、1,655 小时），经场景一致分割、质量过滤、相机位姿估计与事件级字幕标注构建，并显示在其上训练可延长世界模型的生成时程。
AI.relevance_reason: 其长时程连贯性数据构造与「静态场景上下文／动态前景事件」分离、按事件边界对齐的标注方式，可能为 LVR 中长程 latent 状态的维持与事件级监督、贡献分配提供线索，需核查是否可迁移；但论文本身聚焦视频生成数据集，与视觉推理关联较远。
